status: LOCKED - parameters frozen before any result on this dataset was inspected
hypothesis: FX majors mean-revert at multi-day horizons. Every variance ratio measured on audited post-inception H4 data sits at or below 1.0 (AUDUSD 0.909, GBPUSD 0.910, GBPJPY 0.896, USDJPY 0.938, EURUSD 0.962 at q=120), which is the opposite of what V15 assumed. A stretch away from a rolling mean, entered against the move and exited on reversion to that mean, should capture it if the effect is real.
why_this_follows_from_evidence: V15 was refuted precisely because the trend persistence it required is absent. The same measurement that refuted it points weakly the other way: six of six symbols below VR 1.0 at the longest horizon tested. No individual reading is significant at 5%, so this is a hypothesis worth one honest test, not a discovery.

why_these_parameters.timeframe_minutes: 240 (H4). Unchanged from V15 so the two are comparable, and still coarse enough that a ~2 pip round trip is small against an ATR-scaled stop.
why_these_parameters.lookback: 20 - the same window V15 used for its Donchian channel, reused deliberately rather than re-searched. Changing it would make this a second trial.
why_these_parameters.entry_z: 2.0 - two standard deviations is the conventional definition of a stretched move, not a fitted threshold.
why_these_parameters.exit_z: 0.5 - exit on reversion most of the way to the mean; taking the full round trip to 0.0 is greedier and rarely fills.
why_these_parameters.stop_z: 4.0 - twice the entry stretch. A move that doubles its extension has invalidated the premise.
why_these_parameters.max_holding_bars: 60 - ten days at H4. Mean reversion that has not happened in ten days is not going to; without a time stop the strategy silently becomes buy-and-hold.

provenance: Mean reversion in FX is long documented; see Jorda & Taylor (2012) on FX carry and reversal, and the broader statistical-arbitrage literature on Bollinger-style z-score entries. The z-thresholds are textbook values, not search results.
trials_used_for_deflation: Read from research/v15_trials.json at run time. V16 is not a fresh start: it is another specification tried against the same data, and the deflation must account for every earlier one.
data_requirements: Audited, post-inception bars only. EURUSD from 1999-01-04, USDJPY from 1988-07-11, per tools/audit_history.py. Running this on MetaQuotes' synthetic pre-1999 history would repeat the error that made EURUSD look significantly trending.
predeclared_expectation: The variance ratios are not individually significant, so the base rate for this working is low. A FAIL is the expected outcome and will be reported as such; a PASS would need to survive deflation against every trial on record before it means anything.
